newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says too busy to indulge in reshuffle talk.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says too busy to indulge in reshuffle talk.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday there was too much work to be done to pay attention to rumours of a French government reshuffle.
"We've too much work on a day-to-day basis to get into this kind of speculation," he told journalists on the sidelines of a debate on pension funds at the National Assembly.
"The President (Jacques Chirac) has reaffirmed the government's policy is the right one. We have to mobilise and channel our energy into bolstering the economy, growth and employment," he added.
Reshuffle talk is rife in the corridors of parliament, with some media commentators forecasting the replacement of Arthuis and Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre.
Arthuis' office on Thursday denied he was resigning while an official in Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office repeated that a reshuffle was not on the agenda.
